summary: Added joint consensus to the sweep's event set and requested isolated execution of the new bytes. Half of the configuration proposals on node 4 now carry Transition=ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit, so the cluster enters a joint configuration - Voters[0] receives the change while Voters[1] keeps the outgoing voters - and because the implicit transition sets AutoLeave, the leader itself proposes the zero-change leave once the entry is applied, meaning the leave-joint proposal comes from the target's own auto-leave path in appliedTo rather than from the harness. That puts decision formation under a joint quorum (a majority in both halves) inside the event stream, which the previous interpretation recorded as the missing piece. The draft-side run of this revision reports seeds=60, steps_per_seed=60, elections=468, ordinary proposals=460, conf_change_proposals=356 and violations=0, so the four invariants still show no witness with joint transitions present; because that is construction feedback only, the submission asks for a fresh isolated execution and records the changed event set as the revision reason. Still outside the event set and therefore still open in gap 984747de5ed94b4ea8f6977b2a92808f-gap-2: restarts of a node from persisted storage with the applied ConfState carried forward, promotion/demotion of an existing voter rather than the joining node, and the liveness witness for whether the campaign guard's applied-lag condition can leave a cluster without an electable voter.
